hops.note:
Real, public OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec confirmed at github.com/cloudflare/api-schemas, openapi.yaml (18,310,953 bytes as fetched today -- the 16.8MB the ticket cited has already grown, confirming the spec really is updated regularly). Loaded via internal/openapi.Load directly, no redocly_bundle needed -- unlike DigitalOcean, plain Load succeeded against the unbundled document. Re-run today with a fresh scratch tool (candidate-provider-survey.md's own one-shot tool was not committed, so a new one was built, same method: wraps openapi.Load + resourcemap.Discover/DiscoverDataSources, built inside ubx-provider-dynamic's own module tree under cmd/scratch-cf-discover since Go's internal-package visibility rule blocks a separate module even with a replace directive -- deleted after this hop). Real, live counts today: 2150 paths, 307 resources, 721 data sources, 1028 total -- close to but not identical to the survey's own 2123/307/714/1021 (real drift, consistent with a regularly-updated upstream spec, not a discrepancy to chase).

Real finding, new, not covered by anything currently in onboard-provider.md: 34.5% of discovered resources (106/307) and 44.8% of data sources (323/721) have a TypeName matching a generic-response-wrapper pattern (deriveNoun's own response-schema-name heuristic, resourcemap.go's own doc comment calls this 'the strong, real signal' -- weak for Cloudflare specifically). Cloudflare's own spec authors reuse a small set of generic response envelope schema component names (single_response, id_response, single_response_collection, ...) across hundreds of structurally distinct real resources instead of giving each its own uniquely named schema component -- confirmed by reading real examples: cloudflare_access_single_response_2 through _22 are 15 genuinely distinct real Access sub-resources, disambiguated only by an appended collision counter, not a bug in the collision resolution itself. Not a loader gap (the spec loads and produces real, distinct resources) and not a correctness bug (nothing is silently merged that shouldn't be) -- a real, provider-specific naming-quality issue that will make write-artifacts categorization/description authoring materially harder for roughly a third to a half of Cloudflare's own wire types, the same shape of thing hop 3's own DigitalOcean grouping warning already exists to catch early, just one level lower (noun quality within a service, not service grouping itself). Recording here per UBI-222's own explicit instruction to record every point needing intervention as a runbook gap; adding a corresponding check to onboard-provider.md's own hop 3 in the same PR as this manifest, rather than working around it silently.

Distinct operation tags: 551, real and human-authored (Email Security Settings, Radar HTTP, R2 Bucket, Threat Signals, Workers for Platforms, Zone Settings, ...) -- a real, usable grouping signal exists, same shape as DigitalOcean's own tags that namespace_from_tags already reads. Checking whether namespace_from_tags should be enabled for cloudflare is hop 3's own job once the live entry exists (hop 2); noted here as a positive signal, not decided yet.

sdk/providers/.ubx/config carries [dynamic_providers.cloudflare], live: schema_source=openapi, schema_url=github.com/cloudflare/api-schemas' own raw openapi.yaml, base_url from the spec's own declared servers entry (api.cloudflare.com/client/v4), namespace_from_tags=true (see loader-check below for why). No redocly_bundle needed.

Real ubx sdk gen --only cloudflare --dump-ir run against the live entry, real output: 1088 resource type(s), 14,862 real fields, 5,305 sourced (36%), 0 AI-inferred, 9,557 genuinely undescribed (64%). Two real, confirmed-live bugs found and fixed in ubx-provider-dynamic before this succeeded, neither worked around -- see ubx-provider-dynamic PR #59 (open, not merged) for the full account:

1. deriveNoun's path-based fallback crashed the run outright the first time: a data source path ending in a literal '-' segment singularized to an empty string, producing a bare 'cloudflare_' TypeName that failed sdk/codegen/ir's own ServiceAndLocalName ('wire type must be at least <provider>_<service>'). Root cause was general, not a one-off: the fallback's scan started one segment before the read path's own true last segment, correct only when that last segment is always a {param} (true for a single-item resource path, never checked for a collection-shaped data source path). Also silently produced wrong nouns for several real Cloudflare types before the crash was even hit ('ai' instead of 'finetune', 'd1' instead of 'database', 'kv' instead of 'namespace'). Fixed at the root (start the scan at the true last segment), new regression test, real effect: 721 -> 834 real data sources once the run stopped losing 113 of them to a shared wrong noun.

2. The real service/namespace grouping check hop 3 asks for was UNREACHABLE as the runbook and the tool stood: namespace_from_tags (the flag meant to fix exactly this) had no effect at all for a live, unpinned OpenAPI provider -- confirmed by an identical before/after schema.json diff with the flag toggled, then traced to the real cause: the live --dump-namespaces branch returned an unconditional empty map, never reading cfg.NamespaceFromTags, because that flag was only ever wired into the snapshot-GENERATION path (used at hop 4/5), not the live single-provider path every still-live provider actually runs. Fixed at the root so the live path now honors the flag too, mirroring the snapshot path's own real algorithm.

With that fix in hand, the real grouping check: mechanical wire-name split alone produces 362 distinct services from 1088 real wire types, 198 of them (54.7%) single-resource -- the same real fragmentation problem hop 3's own DigitalOcean example describes, confirmed for real on Cloudflare too. Tag-based grouping (namespace_from_tags=true) is a genuine but MIXED real result, unlike DigitalOcean's clean win: 443 distinct namespaces (more than the mechanical split, not fewer -- Cloudflare's own 551 real operation tags are simply finer-grained than its 1088 real wire types support as a clean product taxonomy), but single-resource namespaces drop to 150 (33.9%, down from 54.7%) and the namespace names themselves read as real Cloudflare products more often (r2bucket, cloudflaretunnel, zonesettings, magicconnectors, emailsecuritysettings) than the mechanical split's own coarser, sometimes-generic groups (access, tls, magic, iam, zero, custom, resource). Judgment call, not a clean-cut measurement: enabled (namespace_from_tags=true, see live-entry above) on the strength of the single-resource-fragmentation reduction, the specific problem this check exists to catch, accepting the total-group-count tradeoff -- flagged here explicitly rather than presented as an unambiguous win, for the founder to revisit if write-artifacts finds the tag-based groups less usable in practice than the mechanical ones would have been.
